description: KEY cortex controllers act only on the tenant BusinessGuard checked (R0-07a security review ST-1; COST-LEDGER-001 section 7 items 7, 8, 9). Run from apps/server: npx vitest run test/key-cortex-tenant-binding.integration.test.ts src/core/config/key-cortex-tenant-binding.spec.ts test/ai-direct-provider-503.integration.test.ts --reporter=json --outputFile=.proof/r0-34b-vitest.json against a migrated local database and REDIS_URL, then node ../../scripts/proof-admission/evaluate.mjs --manifest ../../scripts/proof-admission/manifests/key-cortex-tenant-binding.json --report .proof/r0-34b-vitest.json. Every passing case of the three files is required. allowAdditionalCases is true only because the three files carry three it.todo cases outside this write set (key-connector.controller.ts, CommerceVisionService, SemanticMemoryService), which the evaluator would otherwise reject as unexpected; requireReportSuccess keeps every reported case binding. ai-direct-provider-503.integration.test.ts is also bound by optional-services-fail-visibly.json (R0-07a); its case titles are unchanged. RED-BEFORE (claude/elegant-curie-7azpsb at 02234c68, tests-first commit 85b3da7d): the static spec failed 10 of 14 (40 handlers read @Query('businessId'), 1 read the tenant from a whole @Query(), 1 multipart handler read it from the multipart body, 41 lacked @GuardedBusinessId(); KeyCortexDocumentService built its client with 'sk-no-key'; OpenAiVoiceProvider rewrapped the provider 503); the real-database suite failed 17 of 35: with the handler alone, A's owner sending the JSON body {businessId: A} with ?businessId=B got an AiUsageLog row billed to B from voice/speak, B's autonomy profile, goals, trigger rules and sessions, a CortexSession written under B by conscious/stream, and DELETE goals/<B's goal> answered 200 and deleted it; under the production TenantInterceptor the rows stayed in A but every service was handed B and the speak credit check read B's subscription; SUPER_ADMIN naming no tenant reached the phone service with undefined. ai-direct-provider-503 failed 3 of 19 (the three flipped it.todo cases: voice/tts and keyflow voice, and KEY speak/listen, answered 503 with code UNKNOWN_ERROR; the ST-1 split handed this business to KEY voice). The review ST-3 deny cases (401 unauthenticated, 403 non-member, 403 other business on every direct-AI route) and the rewrap-other-errors cases passed before the fix: they are negative controls. REVIEW REPAIR (ST-1, ST-2): the session services read the Redis entry cortex:session:<id> before the tenant-scoped database, so with B's session cached by B's own traffic a member of A naming B's session id read B's messages (GET messages 200) and ran conscious/stream, conscious/chat, chat, chat/stream and stream on B's session; the suite's Redis stand-in always missed, which hid it, and is now an in-memory get/setex store. Five body handlers typed `Dto & { businessId }` are emitted as Object, so the ValidationPipe skipped them and a non-string body businessId reached the service (PATCH triggers/<B's rule> with {businessId:{not:'zz'}} and ?businessId=A disabled B's rule with the handler alone; 500 under the production pipeline). RED-BEFORE the repair (pkt/R0-34b-KEY-TENANT-BINDING at 8bd67385 with the repair tests): 21 failed (3 static, 18 real-database); the warm-cache positive control, the same-tenant session controls and the SUPER_ADMIN body refusals passed (negative controls). After the fix the split cases were tightened from '200 or 403' to the exact status the fix answers (200 acting on A; 404 for B's goal; 403 for the multipart counter-split ?businessId=A with a field naming B, which the base served for A).
